desc:
An alien language uses the lowercase English letters, but in a different alphabetical order. The string order lists all 26 letters from the alien-smallest to the alien-largest.

The string words contains words separated by single commas. Return true if the words appear in non-decreasing order under the alien alphabet, otherwise false. Words are compared like in a dictionary: find the first position where they differ and compare those two letters by their place in order; if one word is a prefix of the other, the shorter one is smaller. Equal neighbours are allowed.

words = "hello,leetcode", order = "hlabcdefgijkmnopqrstuvwxyz"  -> true   (h comes before l)
words = "word,world,row",  order = "worldabcefghijkmnpqstuvxyz"  -> false  ("world" has l at index 3, "word" has d; d is after l)
words = "apple,app",       order = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"  -> false  ("app" is a prefix of "apple" so it must come first)
constraints: order is a permutation of the 26 lowercase letters
words and order consist of lowercase English letters (plus the separating commas)
hints: It is enough to check that every pair of neighbouring words is in order. Why does sortedness of neighbours imply sortedness of all?
Build a lookup rank[letter] from order so you can compare two letters in O(1).
For a neighbouring pair, scan to the first differing position and compare ranks. If there is no differing position within the shorter word, the first word must not be longer than the second.
editorial: The relation 'comes before or equal in the alien dictionary' is transitive, so a list is sorted exactly when each adjacent pair is. For each adjacent pair (a, b) walk along the letters until the first mismatch: if rank[a[k]] > rank[b[k]] the list is not sorted, if smaller the pair is fine. When no mismatch is found within the length of the shorter word, the pair is fine only if len(a) ≤ len(b) (a longer word cannot come before its own prefix).

Building the rank table is O(26) and every adjacent comparison costs at most the word length, so the total is O(total number of letters). A common alternative is to translate every word into ordinary letters using the order (mapping the i-th alien letter to the i-th English letter), after which the list is sorted if and only if it equals its own sorted copy.
